## Lifecycle and threading

after.content:
- `prompt` returns immediately with an `AgentRun`. `completion()` settles after the durable terminal transition. `abort()` is cooperative and idempotent.
- Provider and Tool effects execute off the Session commit boundary on bounded-by-caller/runtime executors. Store writes remain short revision-CAS critical sections.
- Prompt contributors run before a Provider attempt on the effect executor, in deterministic `priority/source/id` order. Each contributor and the assembled prompt have explicit token budgets; one contributor failure is isolated and source provenance remains attached to accepted fragments.
- Local resource scanning is bounded, progressive, cancellable, and single-flight per catalog. Project context, skills, templates, settings and extension metadata remain unavailable until an exact project/resource-set fingerprint is trusted; each load rechecks canonical path/content hash against the discovery generation, and one TOCTOU change invalidates the whole protected projection. Ready snapshots own immutable bytes; the next coalesced refresh detects set membership changes without a duplicate full scan.
- `Flow.Publisher` callbacks run on a Session-owned event executor so slow listeners cannot occupy Provider/Tool effect threads. Each subscriber buffer is bounded at 256 events; producers apply `SubmissionPublisher` backpressure instead of dropping lifecycle events or growing an unbounded queue. Listener failures are isolated by `SubmissionPublisher`.
- All public DTO collections are copied. `transcript()` and Store snapshots are immutable projections, never an alternate fact source.
